# Introduction

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Introduction

The Ford–Fulkerson algorithm addresses the maximum flow problem. It involves finding the greatest possible flow from a source vertex to a sink vertex in a flow network, such that the flow on each edge does not exceed the given capacity.

Imagine you have a large water tank (source) and a garden with several plants that need watering (sink).

The water flows through a system of hoses with different capacities, meaning some hoses can carry more water than others at any given time.

![Real Life Analogy of a Flow Network](data:image/png;base64,)

Now, suppose you want to find out how much liquid can flow from the source to the sink at an instance. How would you do that?

Well, the Ford–Fulkerson algorithm is meant to solve such problems.
